args.summary: Stone age open field sandbox, played through to a Defeat. What worked: the deploy phase, select-all, the minimap jump, the Enemy button, the powers list (Forced March, Rally Cry), the speed buttons and a readable result screen. Problems: (1) Bug: the Attack button plus a tap on the ground did not issue the attack-move. Only a long press worked. (2) Dragging did not pan the camera reliably, and pinch zoom barely moved. (3) My army went from 30% to 0% very fast, and the only rout warning was one 'Hunters shaken' toast. (4) With no army left, the battle ran on as dead time until the enemy burned my camp. Please add a surrender button. (5) The result screen says 76,000 of my men lost and 0 of theirs, which seems odd: we fought for a while and they lost none? The 'Auto is tuned' line is confusing in a sandbox. The Steward button gave no visible panel. Naval was not tested: this session was a land battle.

thought: Result screen reached, it's a defeat. Ending the session.

args.summary:
Bronze age walled-city assault, played to the end: I lost when the 20 minute clock ran out. Naval was the only checklist area I never reached, because this session was a land siege.

What worked:
- The result screen is clear. It shows men lost on both sides, regiments destroyed, auxiliaries trained, the general's fall chance and city damage.
- Arrow Storm and Rally Cry were easy to fire, and the toasts that confirm them read well.
- The win condition text in the top banner ("break in and burn their 9 base buildings") is helpful.

Biggest problems:
- Orders are unreliable. Attack from the long-press radial menu did nothing, and the units stayed idle.
- Arming Attack and then tapping the minimap only moved the camera. No order went out.
- Arming Attack and then tapping a wall tower did work.
- Squads trained during the battle pile up idle at camp, so I kept having to re-select everyone.
- Tapping other camp buildings never opened their own panels, and the camp only trains laborers. I fou

args.summary:
I played three classical sea battles in this sandbox session and won all three. The fleets close fast, the strength bar (You % vs Them %) shows clearly who is winning, the Enemy button jumps the camera to the enemy fleet, and All, Path and Attack work. Drawing a path with the fleet selected worked well.

Main problems:
1. Ships are very hard to select one at a time. Tapping a hull or a health bar often selects nothing. My tap in this last battle missed too, and the fleets were already locked together 11 seconds in.
2. The box drag in Select mode moved the camera instead of selecting.
3. In the naval deploy phase, the chevron makes the Deploy panel bigger instead of hiding it, so the panel covers the ships.
4. The deploy text talks about a keep and squads in a fleet battle.
5. The result screens use land terms: men lost, regiments, and the raw key "attacker (lossesDecisive)".
6. Battles end suddenly, sometimes off screen under the bottom button bar.

Fun is decent, about 3 out of 5, but

thought: Last step. The ships clashed before I could pick one out. Wrapping up the session.

args.summary:
I played three kingdoms-age sack defenses. All three ended too early to really play. The first two ended at exactly 0:44 and the third, against a siege army, at 1:08, each time with "They withdrew from the field". That left no time for workers, buildings or holding the walls.

Bugs:
- Arrow Storm did nothing while paused, even though the pause panel says powers are usable while paused. No strike, no supply spent, and the hint stayed up.
- After I resumed, the result screen came up right after my next tap. Supply was still full, so the strike may never have fired.
- Native dropdowns on touch: a tap on an option fell through and ticked the mercenaries checkbox under it.

What works:
- The setup screen is clear.
- Deploy and Start are easy.
- Select-all and attack-move both work.
- The result screen reads well: men lost, XP per unit, and houses ruined in the city.

Main fix: the raiders' withdraw trigger fires far too early. A siege army should have to grind at the walls.

thought: Wrapping up. Mostly let down by battles that end before they start.

args.summary: Modern walled assault, played through without a winner by the end of the session (You 26% vs Them 28%, their base buildings 7, mine 5). What worked: the goal banner is clear (break in and burn the base buildings), the Artillery Barrage power and the Rally Cry shortcut are readable and quick to use, the gate-breach alert shows up, and 2x speed helps. What hurt: tapping Idle always throws the camera back to my base, so every order to idle squads takes Idle, then Enemy, then Attack it. Panning by dragging is sluggish. The minimap is small and its blue dots are hard to read. Go on the breach banner does not move the camera. Alerts pile up over the top left of the map. The "-60 attrition" chip is never explained. Squads keep going idle in front of the walls instead of pushing through the gate. Compared with Total War sieges, there is no clear breach and push flow. Fun 3.

args.summary: I covered every checklist area. In the information-age sea battles, setup, deploy (All 6 and then a tap in the zone to place), Path drawing and focusing fire with Attack all work. The ships are big and easy to read, and the strength bar (You vs Them) is clear. Problems I found: 1) Naval text still uses land words: the deploy objective says "Take the keep", and the result screens say men, regiments and army. 2) Land powers like Charge have no effect I could see at sea. 3) Numbers disagree: the regiment count doesn't match my ship count, and the battle length doesn't match the clock. 4) The setup screen shows a raw key, "attacker (lossesDecisive)". 5) Tapping a single ship during deploy often doesn't select it. 6) The deploy panel covers the fleet. 7) The speed buttons stay on top of the result panel. Overall the sea fights are short and readable but don't have much depth yet. My last fight was just starting when the session ran out.

args.summary: I played the future-age sack defense to the end and lost. The defeat came down to one last raider tank. My infantry would not fire at it with an armed Attack order. A plain tap moved them in, but they still did no damage. Three artillery barrages barely scratched it, so I could not finish the raiders before the clock ran out, even though I was well ahead in men lost (68% of theirs against 14% of mine... I mean 31% of mine). The burn limit was only 2 houses and the game never said so up front. What works: the result screen is easy to read (men lost, XP per unit, city damage), aiming the powers is clear, and the Idle and Enemy HUD buttons help find units. The speed buttons work well too. When you come back to setup it keeps your last picks, but the Fight button is below the fold on a landscape phone. Top fixes: let infantry damage tanks, or tell me clearly when they can't. Show the win and loss rules (burn limit, clock) at deploy. Make the Attack order give feedback when it is dropped.

thought: I'm ending the session. The battle could not be won because of the tank, and that soured an otherwise readable fight.
